transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Leon Chen (Redwood SE), Amir Patel (Orion - Head of ML), Carla Gomez (Orion - Infra), Dan Lee (Orion - Security)

Auto-generated summary: quick POC scoping to decide hosted vs dedicated vs private, align on success criteria, workload size for benchmarks, timelines and security checklist.

Topics: success criteria, throughput & latency targets, sample workload, dataset size, benchmark plan, network/VPC requirements, SOC2/KMS questions, timeline and next steps.

00:00 Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, im Sofia AE on the Redwood side, and Leon here is our solutions engineer.
00:18 Leon: hi all, hi Amir, Carla, Dan, thanks for having us. we thought we'd run through the high level decision criteria between hosted, dedicated and private and then scope the POC benchmarks you want.
00:30 Amir: thanks, im Amir. short background - we run a realtime risk scoring API for payments, about 3k qps at peak, most requests short sequences but some long context for dispute workflows, latency budget 100-200ms p50 and 300-500ms p95 depending on model. cost is also a hard constraint, we cant 3x infra cost.
00:55 Carla: infra questions - we have VPC peering and strict egress rules, need to know if Redwood hosted can meet our compliance, or if we must go dedicated or private.
01:10 Dan: and from security we need SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration and SAML SSO for console, plus data residency for EU customers.
01:25 Leon: yep understood. quick framing, hosted (Redwood API) is fastest to launch with usage pricing, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput with SLA, private (VPC or on-prem) gives full network isolation and customer-managed keys. tradeoffs are speed to market vs control and cost predictability.
01:50 Sofia: for the POC we usually test two configs: hosted at first to validate model quality and baseline latency/cost, then a dedicated profile to validate throughput at scale, and optionally a private deployment if there are blocking compliance constraints.
02:10 Amir: can you run benchmarks using our sample queries? we want to see p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens anchored to our workload.
02:25 Leon: absolutely, we will need sample query set, expected concurrency, and any golden responses for quality checks. for throughput testing we ask for a representative mix and size distribution, e g 70% short, 25% medium, 5% long.
02:40 Amir: yep we can provide that. rough numbers: 3k qps peak, average tokens per request 120, tail up to 2k.
02:55 Leon: perfect. for dedicated sizing that likely maps to a few reserved GPU nodes depending on model and quantization. we will run runs on a small dedicated pool then scale to your peak to measure batching efficiency and KV cache hit rates.
03:15 Sofia: success criteria we recommend capturing three buckets - latency/throughput SLOs, cost per inference (or per token), and quality/regression against golden set. also operational items: SSO, audit logs, network topology.
03:35 Amir: we're most concerned with maintaining quality - can't have hallucinations on risk scores - and staying inside our latency SLOs. cost target is within 1.5x our current baseline.
03:50 Leon: noted. also if you plan private deployment, timeline expands because we need network validation, KMS exchange, and maybe on-prem hardware coordination. typically private POC takes 4-8 weeks, dedicated 2-4 weeks, hosted can be immediate as long as data residency and contract ok.
04:15 Carla: clarify the KMS flow - we use cloud KMS, do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
04:25 Leon: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integration. Dedicated also supports customer-managed keys for data-at-rest on dedicated instances, and we can provide connectivity for envelope encryption. hosted supports encryption in transit and at rest but for strict KMS requirements we often recommend dedicated or private.
04:45 Dan: about audit logs and retention - we need to retain request logs for 13 months. is that possible?
04:55 Sofia: we can support extended log retention as an add-on, Redwood Console provides per-route tracing and token-level breakdowns, and we can export logs to your SIEM.
05:10 Leon: on benchmarks, we'll run two main experiments: 1) latency profile for your median and tail across hosted vs dedicated; 2) throughput scaling test on dedicated to validate concurrency and batching. we also measure cost per token for each config.
05:30 Amir: what's the typical difference people see in tail latency hosted vs dedicated?
05:35 Leon: usually dedicated reduces p95 by 15-40% depending on batch behavior and kernel selection. also quantization choices influence CPU/GPU usage; smaller quantized models mean cheaper per token but may affect quality.
05:55 Sofia: we should capture model variants to test: the one you prefer for quality, plus a quantized variant for cost testing.
06:05 Amir: ok that'll work. next the network - we need to know IPs and egress flows to open firewall rules for hosted testing, and if dedicated, we may do VPC peering.
06:20 Carla: for hosted tests we dont want any customer data leaving EU. can hosted API be restricted to eu region and comply with data residency?
06:30 Sofia: yes hosted supports region pins; we can run requests from EU region. however for strict residency and customer-managed keys, private is the only full guarantee.
06:45 Dan: any SOC2 or ISO docs you can share now?
06:50 Sofia: yes i'll share SOC2 and our network diagram after the call, also a short security FAQ.
07:00 Leon: on measurement details - please provide a golden set and quality thresholds, we'll run hypothesis tests between model variants and report regressions. we also track KV cache hit rates because that can change latency dramatically for repeated prefixes.
07:25 Amir: that KV cache thing - we've got a lot of repeated session prefixes so cache hit rate could help a lot. what's the recommendation there?
07:35 Leon: for sessiony workloads with repeated context, both hosted with caching and dedicated with persistent KV store help. in dedicated you can tune cache shards for lower latency; private gives even more control if you want to manage caches locally.
07:55 Sofia: timeline recapped - Sofia sends pricing & contract outline within 48 hours; Leon to send benchmark plan and required test harness; Amir to provide data and golden responses; Carla to share network constraints and open firewall ticket. we aim to start hosted baseline runs within 1 week and dedicated benchmarks in 2-3 weeks pending network.
08:25 Amir: are there known blockers that typically push customers to private?
08:30 Leon: yes usually regulatory constraints around KMS, strict data residency, and on-prem hardware requirements. cost alone rarely forces private unless they already have major infra investments.
08:45 Dan: procurement question - if we do dedicated, is there an enterprise contract and SLA?
08:50 Sofia: yes dedicated comes with reserved capacity contracts and SLA backed uptime and latency targets; we'll attach the SLA summary in the packet.
09:00 Amir: for the POC, can you estimate cost for running 1M inference tokens in hosted vs dedicated for our config?
09:07 Leon: we'll include a worked example in the worksheet but ballpark hosted might be higher per token at low volume; dedicated amortizes over reserved capacity and can be cheaper at steady high throughput. exact numbers will be in the price capacity worksheet.
09:25 Sofia: any competitors you are also considering?
09:28 Amir: yup we're looking at Anthropic for models and also evaluating AWS Bedrock for vendor lock in concerns.
09:35 Leon: understood, we'll highlight areas where Redwood's smart routing, KV caching and quantization recommendations affect unit economics.
09:45 Sofia: ok quick recap and explicit next steps - action items aligned in the doc and i'll follow up with an email that includes SOC2, network diagram, pricing worksheet and a proposed schedule.
09:58 Amir: sounds good, thanks. one more ask - can we see a sample benchmark report from a previous dedicated POC?
10:05 Leon: yes i'll anonymize and send a sample perf report and the scripts we use.
10:12 Carla: thanks everyone, that helps.
10:20 Sofia: great, we'll get the artifacts out and circle back. thanks everyone.
